Dean Ocean Abrams

No Party Affiliation candidate for Governor and Lieutenant Governor, Florida · Open seat

Enterprise technology and management consultant (per his campaign); one third-party profile lists him as a Sarasota real estate agent

Dean Ocean Abrams is a Sarasota resident running for Florida governor with No Party Affiliation. His running mate is Joe Van Vactor. He filed with the Florida Division of Elections on April 16, 2026, paid the qualifying fee, and qualified on June 11, 2026.

Where Abrams stands

Property taxes
Proposes ending property taxes on homesteaded homes valued at up to 200% of the county median, with smaller cuts above that level. Says each tax cut should come with published replacement math.
Property tax structure
Supports Amendment 3, which raises the homestead exemption and cuts the non-homestead assessment cap to 5%. Objects to its five-year wait for later arrivals and would set up a public replacement commission.
Property insurance
Proposes capping insurer profit, requiring whole-company accounting that includes affiliates, returning surplus to policyholders, publishing insurer loss ratios and rate justifications, and expanding My Safe Florida Home.
Housing
Proposes barring institutional investors from buying single-family homes in Florida, with exemptions for builders, land trusts, nonprofits and small local landlords. Supports just-cause eviction and 90 days' notice for rent increases above 5%.
Affordability / cost of living
Names affordability as a main focus, saying rising costs, taxes and insurance rates have put housing and healthcare out of reach for Floridians.
Immigration
Says due process is not open borders. Supports enforcing valid law against violent offenders and traffickers and holding accountable employers who exploit unauthorized labor.
Guns / Second Amendment
Says he supports constitutional carry, which is already Florida law, and supports open carry.
Criminal justice / prison reform
Proposes requiring police body cameras to be on and recording for every interaction with the public, with no option to switch them off mid-encounter.
Education / school choice
Says not every student needs a four-year degree and that Florida needs the workers produced by non-degree programs.
Healthcare
Would direct the state health care agency to seek a waiver to cover about 800,000 Floridians in the coverage gap. Supports extending enhanced ACA credits as a bridge and starting the state's drug importation program.

Background

  • Candidate for Florida governor (NPA), 2026; filed 04/16/2026, qualified 06/11/2026
  • Changed party registration from Republican to NPA in 2022 (per WUSF)
  • Career in enterprise technology and management consulting, including at Microsoft, HP and KPMG (per his campaign)
  • Helped rebuild New York City first-responder emergency communications after September 11 (per his campaign)
  • Lives in Sarasota; age 50 (per WKMG/ClickOrlando voter guide)
